etymology: Scholarly designation for John 13-17 — Jesus' upper-room teaching the night before the cross.
biblical_def: Jesus' extended upper-room teaching (John 13-17) including foot-washing, the new commandment, the True Vine, the promise of the Spirit, and the high-priestly prayer.
webster_summary: Jesus' upper-room teaching of John 13-17.
webster_full: The extended teaching by Jesus in the upper room on the night of His arrest, recorded in John 13-17: foot-washing, new commandment, declaration of the way-truth-life, promise of another Comforter, the True Vine teaching, and the high-priestly prayer.
scriptures: John 14:6
Jesus saith unto him, I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.
John 14:26
But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things.
John 17:3
And this is life eternal, that they might know thee the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom thou hast sent.
corruption_summary: Mined for individual sermon-verses, missing the unified flow as Jesus' last instruction to His disciples.
corruption_paragraphs: John 13-17 is one block. Read straight through, it is the Lord preparing His own for life without His physical presence — promising another Comforter, teaching union as a Vine, praying them safe to the Father. Read it as one breath.
usage: Read John 13-17 as one continuous discourse.
It is Jesus preparing His own for absence.

etymology: From Latin ascendere "to climb up."
biblical_def: The bodily ascension of the risen Christ from the Mount of Olives forty days after the resurrection, to the Father's right hand, where He reigns and intercedes (Acts 1:9-11; Eph 1:20-22).
webster_summary: Christ's bodily return to the Father's right hand.
webster_full: The bodily ascension of the risen Christ from the Mount of Olives forty days after the resurrection, witnessed by the apostles, to His present session at the right hand of the Father in heaven, where He reigns over all and intercedes for His people.
scriptures: Acts 1:9
And when he had spoken these things, while they beheld, he was taken up; and a cloud received him out of their sight.
Ephesians 1:20-22
He raised him from the dead, and set him at his own right hand in the heavenly places... and hath put all things under his feet.
Hebrews 4:14
Seeing then that we have a great high priest, that is passed into the heavens, Jesus the Son of God.
corruption_summary: Treated as Easter's footnote rather than the climactic enthronement of the Mediator King.
corruption_paragraphs: Resurrection without ascension leaves Christ wandering the earth; ascension is His enthronement. He sits at the right hand because the work is done. Acts 1, Ephesians 1, Hebrews 1 all proclaim the same coronation. Recover the Ascension.
usage: Ascension is the enthronement of the King.
He sits — the work is done.

etymology: Greek hēmera kyriou — day of the Lord; New Testament fulfillment of Old Testament prophetic theme.
biblical_def: The eschatological day of Christ's return in glory bringing judgment and salvation; in the New Testament identified with the second coming of Jesus (1 Thess 5:2; 2 Pet 3:10; 1 Cor 1:8).
webster_summary: Christ's eschatological day of return.
webster_full: The eschatological day of Christ's return — bringing the judgment of the wicked, the deliverance of the faithful, and the consummation of the kingdom; the Old Testament 'day of YHWH' fully identified with the parousia of the Lord Jesus.
scriptures: 1 Thessalonians 5:2
For yourselves know perfectly that the day of the Lord so cometh as a thief in the night.
2 Peter 3:10
But the day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night; in the which the heavens shall pass away with a great noise.
1 Corinthians 1:8
Who shall also confirm you unto the end, that ye may be blameless in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.
corruption_summary: Reduced to Sunday-the-Lord's-day, blunting the eschatological force of the New Testament usage.
corruption_paragraphs: The Day of the Lord is not the weekly Lord's Day — it is the climactic day of Christ's return. Old Testament prophets pointed to it; New Testament writers locate it in Jesus' parousia. Live in light of the Day.
usage: The Day comes as a thief; be ready.
Sunday is the Lord's Day; the Day of the Lord is yet to come.

etymology: Greek kainē Hierousalēm — the eschatological city of God.
biblical_def: The eschatological city descending from heaven, the bride of Christ adorned for her husband, the eternal dwelling of God with His people (Rev 21:1-22:5).
webster_summary: The eternal city of God descending from heaven.
webster_full: The eschatological holy city descending from heaven in Revelation 21-22 — adorned as a bride, walled with twelve foundations of the apostles and twelve gates of the tribes, lit by the glory of God and the Lamb, with the river of life and the tree of life.
scriptures: Revelation 21:2
And I John saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.
Revelation 21:22-23
I saw no temple therein: for the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are the temple of it. And the city had no need of the sun... for the glory of God did lighten it, and the Lamb is the light thereof.
Hebrews 11:10
For he looked for a city which hath foundations, whose builder and maker is God.
corruption_summary: Reduced to a vague heaven-image; missing the architectural concreteness of Revelation's vision.
corruption_paragraphs: The New Jerusalem is not floating clouds. It is a city — gates, walls, river, tree, throne, bride. The eschaton is urban, not ethereal. Read Revelation 21-22 slowly to recover the city we are heading home to.
usage: Read Revelation 21-22 as architecture.
The eternal city is concrete, not vague.

etymology: Greek antichristos — "against / in place of Christ."
biblical_def: The eschatological adversary opposing Christ and exalting himself as Christ; in John, both the eschatological one and the spirit of antichrist already at work in many (1 John 2:18, 22; 4:3; 2 John 7).
webster_summary: The eschatological adversary impersonating Christ.
webster_full: The eschatological adversary opposing Christ and seeking to take His place by deception; in 1 and 2 John, both a final figure to come and a present spirit at work in those denying that Jesus is the Christ come in flesh; identified by Paul as 'the man of sin' (2 Thess 2:3-4).
scriptures: 1 John 2:18
Little children, it is the last time: and as ye have heard that antichrist shall come, even now are there many antichrists.
1 John 4:3
Every spirit that confesseth not that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is not of God: and this is that spirit of antichrist.
2 Thessalonians 2:3-4
Except there come a falling away first, and that man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition; who opposeth and exalteth himself above all that is called God.
corruption_summary: Reduced to apocalyptic horror-show speculation, missing John's pastoral point about the spirit of antichrist already at work.
corruption_paragraphs: John does not invite us to identify Antichrist; he invites us to identify the spirit of antichrist — denial of the incarnation. Whoever denies that Jesus is the Christ come in flesh is in the antichrist stream. Discernment is more urgent than prediction.
roots_summary: Greek antichristos — against / in place of Christ.
usage: The spirit of antichrist denies the incarnation.
Discernment over prediction.

etymology: Greek thērion — "wild beast," the Apocalypse's symbol of imperial-religious power.
biblical_def: The two beasts of Revelation 13: the first from the sea (political-imperial blasphemy) and the second from the earth (religious deception serving the first); together opposing the Lamb (Rev 13).
webster_summary: Revelation's two beasts: imperial and religious.
webster_full: The two figures of Revelation 13: the first beast rising from the sea — political-imperial power blaspheming God and warring against the saints — and the second from the earth — false-religious power performing signs to compel worship of the first; together the great anti-Lamb coalition.
scriptures: Revelation 13:1
And I stood upon the sand of the sea, and saw a beast rise up out of the sea, having seven heads and ten horns.
Revelation 13:11
And I beheld another beast coming up out of the earth; and he had two horns like a lamb, and he spake as a dragon.
Revelation 13:16-17
He causeth all... to receive a mark in their right hand, or in their foreheads.
corruption_summary: Read as a code to crack instead of as a perpetually applicable pattern of imperial-religious idolatry.
corruption_paragraphs: Whatever specific historical fulfillment Revelation 13 has, the pattern recurs: political power demanding ultimate allegiance with religious sanction, persecuting saints who confess the Lamb. Read the Beast typologically and you see it in many ages, including our own.
usage: Read the Beast as recurring pattern.
Imperial-religious idolatry is perennial.

etymology: Greek Babylōn — symbolic name for the persecuting world-system; rooted in OT historical Babylon.
biblical_def: The symbolic name in Revelation for the worldly economic-religious system arrayed against the Lamb — Mystery Babylon the Great, Mother of Harlots — destined for sudden fall (Rev 17-18).
webster_summary: Revelation's symbol for the world-system opposed to the Lamb.
webster_full: The symbolic name applied in Revelation 17-18 to the worldly economic-religious-political system that intoxicates nations with luxury and persecutes the saints — 'Mystery Babylon the Great, Mother of Harlots' — destined for sudden fall and the rejoicing of heaven.
scriptures: Revelation 17:5
And upon her forehead was a name written, MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF HARLOTS AND ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH.
Revelation 18:2
Babylon the great is fallen, is fallen, and is become the habitation of devils.
Revelation 18:4
Come out of her, my people, that ye be not partakers of her sins.
corruption_summary: Read as code for one specific city or institution; missing how the symbol applies to every age's worldly system.
corruption_paragraphs: Babylon is whatever world-system seduces with luxury and demands compromise. Old Babylon, Rome, modern materialist consumerism — each takes the form of Babylon. The command stands across ages: come out of her, my people.
usage: Come out of Babylon, my people.
Babylon is whichever system seduces and persecutes.

etymology: From Old French herlot "vagabond"; Greek pornē — prostitute.
biblical_def: The biblical figure of unfaithful Israel and, in Revelation, the persecuting world-system: 'the great whore that sitteth upon many waters' arrayed in luxury, drunken with the blood of saints (Rev 17:1-6).
webster_summary: The unfaithful covenant-bride; the world-system's seduction.
webster_full: A repeated biblical figure for unfaithfulness to the covenant — used by the prophets (Hosea, Jeremiah, Ezekiel) for Israel, and in Revelation for the apocalyptic Babylon arrayed in luxury and drunken with the blood of saints, contrasted with the bride of the Lamb.
scriptures: Hosea 1:2
Go, take unto thee a wife of whoredoms and children of whoredoms: for the land hath committed great whoredom, departing from the LORD.
Ezekiel 16:32
But as a wife that committeth adultery, which taketh strangers instead of her husband!
Revelation 17:1-2
Come hither; I will shew unto thee the judgment of the great whore that sitteth upon many waters: with whom the kings of the earth have committed fornication.
corruption_summary: Reduced to a misogynist trope rather than understood as the prophets' device for spiritual unfaithfulness.
corruption_paragraphs: The harlot is not about women — it is the prophets' image for spiritual unfaithfulness. Israel as bride goes whoring; the world-system as Babylon plays the harlot. The bride of the Lamb stands as the redeemed answer. The figure preaches faithfulness.
usage: The harlot is unfaithfulness embodied.
The bride of the Lamb is its redeemed answer.

etymology: Apocalyptic number from Revelation 7 and 14; 12 × 12 × 1000.
biblical_def: The sealed multitude of Revelation 7:1-8 (twelve thousand from each tribe of Israel) and 14:1-5 (with the Lamb on Mount Zion); a symbolic number for the redeemed of God.
webster_summary: Revelation's symbolic number of the sealed.
webster_full: The 144,000 sealed servants of God in Revelation 7 (12,000 from each of the twelve tribes of Israel) and the same number standing with the Lamb on Mount Zion in Revelation 14; a deliberately structured symbolic number — twelve squared times a thousand — representing the complete number of the redeemed.
scriptures: Revelation 7:4
And I heard the number of them which were sealed: and there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel.
Revelation 14:1
And I looked, and, lo, a Lamb stood on the mount Sion, and with him an hundred forty and four thousand, having his Father's name written in their foreheads.
Revelation 7:9
After this I beheld, and, lo, a great multitude, which no man could number.
corruption_summary: Read literalistically by sects (Jehovah's Witnesses, Mormons), missing the symbolic structure of apocalyptic number.
corruption_paragraphs: Twelve squared times a thousand — the number is built. Apocalyptic numbers are not census figures. The 144,000 and the great multitude no man can number are arguably the same group seen from different angles: complete and innumerable at once.
usage: Read 144,000 as symbolic completeness.
The same multitude is innumerable to any human counter.

etymology: Greek phialai — bowls or vials.
biblical_def: The seven final judgments of Revelation 16, poured out from heavenly bowls — boils, blood, scorching heat, darkness, demonic frogs, Armageddon — completing God's wrath on the unrepentant.
webster_summary: Revelation's seven final wrath-judgments.
webster_full: The seven final climactic judgments of Revelation 16, poured out from heavenly bowls (or vials in KJV) by the seven angels — boils, sea-to-blood, rivers-to-blood, scorching sun, darkness, drying of the Euphrates, and the great earthquake; completing God's wrath.
scriptures: Revelation 15:7
And one of the four beasts gave unto the seven angels seven golden vials full of the wrath of God.
Revelation 16:1
Go your ways, and pour out the vials of the wrath of God upon the earth.
Revelation 16:17
And the seventh angel poured out his vial into the air; and there came a great voice out of the temple of heaven... saying, It is done.
corruption_summary: Read with morbid speculation rather than received as the Bible's serious teaching about wrath fully poured out.
corruption_paragraphs: The bowls are not entertainment; they are the climactic exhibition of divine wrath. Whether read futurist, historicist, or idealist, the lesson stands: God's patience has an end, and when it ends, the bowls fully pour. Live now in repentance.
usage: Read Revelation 16 sober.
Wrath fully poured comes after long patience.

etymology: Greek sphragides — seals on the scroll of Revelation 5-8.
biblical_def: The seven seals of the scroll, opened by the Lamb in Revelation 5-8 — four horsemen, martyrs under the altar, cosmic upheaval, and silence in heaven.
webster_summary: The seven seals opened by the Lamb.
webster_full: The seven seals on the scroll of God's purposes, which only the slain Lamb is found worthy to open in Revelation 5; their successive opening unleashes the four horsemen (conquest, war, famine, death), the cry of the martyrs, cosmic upheaval, and a great silence in heaven.
scriptures: Revelation 5:5
Behold, the Lion of the tribe of Juda, the Root of David, hath prevailed to open the book, and to loose the seven seals thereof.
Revelation 6:1-2
I saw when the Lamb opened one of the seals... and behold a white horse: and he that sat on him had a bow.
Revelation 8:1
And when he had opened the seventh seal, there was silence in heaven about the space of half an hour.
corruption_summary: Read as code about specific historical events; missing the deeper theology that only the slain Lamb opens history.
corruption_paragraphs: Revelation 5 is the climax of the throne-room: who is worthy to open the scroll of God's plan? Only the Lamb that was slain. The seals are not first about timing — they are first about who controls history. The Lamb does.
usage: The Lamb opens history's seals.
Read Revelation 5 before Revelation 6.

etymology: Greek salpinges — trumpets sounded by the seven angels in Revelation 8-11.
biblical_def: The seven trumpets blown by the seven angels in Revelation 8-11, unleashing intermediate judgments on a third of earth, sea, rivers, and luminaries; followed by woes including locusts and demonic horsemen.
webster_summary: Revelation's seven middle judgments via trumpet.
webster_full: The seven trumpet-judgments of Revelation 8-11, intermediate between the seals and the bowls, falling on a third of earth, sea, rivers, and heavenly bodies, then the demonic locusts, the army from the Euphrates, and the proclamation of the kingdom at the seventh trumpet.
scriptures: Revelation 8:6
And the seven angels which had the seven trumpets prepared themselves to sound.
Revelation 9:1
And the fifth angel sounded, and I saw a star fall from heaven unto the earth: and to him was given the key of the bottomless pit.
Revelation 11:15
And the seventh angel sounded; and there were great voices in heaven, saying, The kingdoms of this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord, and of his Christ.
corruption_summary: Read as alarming spectacle rather than as God's structured warnings before the final wrath.
corruption_paragraphs: The seven trumpets are warnings calling to repentance — partial judgments (a third, not all) with space yet to repent. The seventh trumpet is the kingdom announcement. Read the trumpets as escalating call before the bowls.
usage: The trumpets warn before the bowls.
The seventh trumpet announces the kingdom.

etymology: Greek epistolai — letters; the seven dictated to the seven Asian churches in Revelation 2-3.
biblical_def: The seven letters Christ dictated to John for the churches of Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia, and Laodicea; each addressing specific commendations, complaints, calls, and conquering-promises (Rev 2-3).
webster_summary: Christ's seven letters to the churches of Asia.
webster_full: The seven letters dictated by the risen Christ for delivery to the seven Asian churches — Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia, Laodicea — each following a deliberate pattern (commendation, complaint, command, conquering-promise) and applicable to the churches of every age.
scriptures: Revelation 1:11
I am Alpha and Omega, the first and the last: and, What thou seest, write in a book, and send it unto the seven churches which are in Asia.
Revelation 2:7
He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches.
Revelation 3:20
Behold, I stand at the door, and knock: if any man hear my voice, and open the door, I will come in to him.
corruption_summary: Read as scolding rather than as Christ's earnest pastoral correspondence to His churches.
corruption_paragraphs: The seven letters are the risen Lord pastoring His churches. Each begins with a self-revelation drawn from Revelation 1, addresses the church's specific situation, and closes with a conquering-promise from Revelation 21-22. Read them as Christ's pastoral mail.
usage: Read the seven letters as pastoral correspondence.
Each letter is to all the churches.

etymology: Greek Hadēs — "the unseen," the realm of the dead.
biblical_def: The intermediate realm of the dead in New Testament usage; in Christ's mouth the place where the rich man suffered (Luke 16); ultimately cast into the lake of fire (Rev 20:14).
webster_summary: The realm of the dead awaiting resurrection.
webster_full: The Greek term used in the New Testament (translating Hebrew Sheol in the Septuagint) for the realm of the dead — the intermediate state where souls await resurrection; ultimately itself cast into the lake of fire at the final judgment.
scriptures: Luke 16:23
And in hell (hadēs) he lift up his eyes, being in torments, and seeth Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom.
Acts 2:27
Because thou wilt not leave my soul in hell (hadēs), neither wilt thou suffer thine Holy One to see corruption.
Revelation 20:14
And death and hell (hadēs) were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death.
corruption_summary: Conflated with Gehenna (lake of fire), erasing the distinction between intermediate and final state.
corruption_paragraphs: Hades is the intermediate state; Gehenna is the final lake of fire. Hades itself is cast into Gehenna at the end. Maintaining the distinction preserves Scripture's careful eschatological order. KJV translates both as 'hell' which loses the precision.
usage: Distinguish Hades (intermediate) from Gehenna (final).
Hades itself is cast into the lake of fire.

etymology: Greek Geenna, from Hebrew gei-Hinnom — Valley of Hinnom, where children were burned to Molech (Jer 7:31; 19:6); used by Christ for final judgment.
biblical_def: Christ's primary term for the place of final eternal punishment, drawn from the Valley of Hinnom outside Jerusalem where idolatrous child-sacrifice occurred and which became a smouldering refuse pit (Matt 5:22, 29-30; 10:28; 23:33).
webster_summary: Christ's term for the place of final punishment.
webster_full: The term Jesus uses for the place of final eternal punishment, drawn from the Valley of Hinnom outside Jerusalem — historically the site of idolatrous child sacrifice to Molech and later a continually smouldering refuse pit — appearing in Matthew, Mark, Luke, and James.
scriptures: Matthew 5:22
Whosoever shall say, Thou fool, shall be in danger of hell fire (geenna).
Matthew 10:28
Fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell (geenna).
Mark 9:43
If thy hand offend thee, cut it off: it is better for thee to enter into life maimed, than having two hands to go into hell (geenna).
corruption_summary: Diluted by 'hell' translations that conflate it with hades, missing how specifically Christ uses it for the final lake of fire.
corruption_paragraphs: Jesus speaks more about Gehenna than anyone else in Scripture. The valley where children were burned to Molech becomes the figure for final judgment. Whatever softer doctrines tempt us, Christ's vocabulary stands. Read the Gehenna sayings sober.
usage: Heed Christ's Gehenna sayings.
Distinguish Gehenna (final) from Hades (intermediate).

etymology: Greek tetelestai (τετέλεσται) — perfect passive of teleō — "it is finished, it stands accomplished."
biblical_def: Jesus' final word from the cross (John 19:30) — "It is finished" — declaring the saving work fully accomplished. Greek perfect tense: completed action with abiding effect.
webster_summary: Jesus' final cry: "It is finished, completely."
webster_full: The Greek verb form Jesus uttered as His final word from the cross, recorded in John 19:30; perfect passive — completed and standing-completed; commercial papyri use it for paid-in-full receipts. The cross declares the saving work finished.
scriptures: John 19:30
When Jesus therefore had received the vinegar, he said, It is finished: and he bowed his head, and gave up the ghost.
Hebrews 10:14
For by one offering he hath perfected for ever them that are sanctified.
Romans 8:1
There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus.
corruption_summary: Reduced to 'I am dying' rather than received as the doctrinal declaration of completed atonement.
corruption_paragraphs: Tetelestai is not a sigh — it is a verdict. Greek receipts read tetelestai for 'paid in full.' The cross is not the beginning of salvation; it is its declaration of completion. Whatever you add to it diminishes it.
usage: The cross says paid-in-full.
Add nothing to tetelestai.

etymology: Term for the council ruling of Acts 15.
biblical_def: The decision issued by the Jerusalem Council (Acts 15) that Gentile converts need not be circumcised but should abstain from food sacrificed to idols, blood, things strangled, and sexual immorality.
webster_summary: The Jerusalem Council's ruling on Gentile inclusion.
webster_full: The decision of the Jerusalem Council recorded in Acts 15: Gentile converts to Christianity are not required to be circumcised or keep the Mosaic law but are asked to abstain from food sacrificed to idols, from blood, from things strangled, and from fornication — to keep table-fellowship with Jewish believers possible.
scriptures: Wherefore my sentence is, that we trouble not them, which from among the Gentiles are turned to God: But that we write unto them, that they abstain from pollutions of idols, and from fornication, and from things strangled, and from blood.
It seemed good to the Holy Ghost, and to us, to lay upon you no greater burden than these necessary things.
Galatians 2:9
When James, Cephas, and John, who seemed to be pillars, perceived the grace that was given unto me, they gave to me and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship.
corruption_summary: Treated as obsolete, missing the lasting principle of charitable accommodation for fellowship's sake.
corruption_paragraphs: The decree's specific clauses target table-fellowship between Jewish and Gentile believers. The principle survives: in matters of conscience, accommodate for fellowship's sake without compromising the gospel. Acts 15 is a model of theological clarity with pastoral charity.
usage: Read Acts 15 for theological-pastoral wisdom.
Charity for fellowship; clarity on the gospel.

etymology: Matthew's church-discipline-and-forgiveness chapter, ~AD 60.
biblical_def: Matthew's chapter on greatness as childlikeness, the lost sheep, the four-step process of church discipline (vv 15-20), and unlimited forgiveness (vv 21-35).
webster_summary: The church-discipline-and-forgiveness chapter.
webster_full: The chapter of Matthew gathering Jesus' teaching on greatness as childlikeness, the urgency of avoiding offenses, the parable of the lost sheep, the fourfold process of restoration (vv 15-20), and the parable of the unforgiving servant teaching unlimited mutual forgiveness.
scriptures: Matthew 18:15
Moreover if thy brother shall trespass against thee, go and tell him his fault between thee and him alone.
Matthew 18:18
Whatsoever ye shall bind on earth shall be bound in heaven.
Matthew 18:21-22
Lord, how oft shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? till seven times? Jesus saith unto him, I say not unto thee, Until seven times: but, Until seventy times seven.
corruption_summary: Read piecemeal — discipline without forgiveness, or forgiveness without discipline — missing the chapter's careful integration of both.
corruption_paragraphs: Matthew 18 holds discipline and forgiveness together. The same chapter that gives the four-step process (vv 15-20) demands the seventy-times-seven heart (vv 21-35). Discipline without forgiveness is harshness; forgiveness without discipline is enabling. The chapter requires both.
usage: Read Matthew 18 whole; do not split it.
Discipline and forgiveness require each other.

etymology: Greek kleides tēs basileias — Matthew 16:19.
biblical_def: The keys given to Peter (and through him to the church) representing the authority to declare what the gospel binds and looses regarding sin and inclusion (Matt 16:19; 18:18; John 20:23).
webster_summary: Authority to declare gospel-binding and loosing.
webster_full: The keys given by Christ to Peter and through him to the assembled church (Matt 16:19; 18:18; John 20:23) — the authority to bind and loose by declaring on earth what heaven has already determined regarding sin, inclusion, and ministry; exercised through faithful preaching and discipline.
scriptures: Matthew 16:19
And I will give unto thee the keys of the kingdom of heaven: and whatsoever thou shalt bind on earth shall be bound in heaven.
Matthew 18:18
Whatsoever ye shall bind on earth shall be bound in heaven: and whatsoever ye shall loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven.
John 20:23
Whose soever sins ye remit, they are remitted unto them; and whose soever sins ye retain, they are retained.
corruption_summary: Either claimed as papal monopoly or denied entirely; missing the Reformed understanding that the keys are exercised through preaching and church discipline.
corruption_paragraphs: The keys are not magic; they are the gospel-authority to declare bound or loosed by reference to Christ's word. Reformed theology distinguishes the keys of preaching (proclamation) and of discipline (admission/exclusion). Both are church-authority, not personal.
usage: Preach and discipline as exercise of the keys.
The keys are shared, not personal.

etymology: Greek petros (πέτρος) — "stone"; petra (πέτρα) — "rock, bedrock."
biblical_def: The wordplay in Matthew 16:18 — "thou art Petros (stone), and upon this petra (bedrock) I will build my church" — distinguishing Peter the man from the foundation, which Reformed exegesis identifies as the confession of Christ.
webster_summary: The Matthew 16:18 wordplay: stone vs. bedrock.
webster_full: The deliberate Greek wordplay in Matthew 16:18: petros (a stone, masculine) and petra (bedrock, feminine). Reformed and Eastern exegesis identifies the petra not with Peter himself but with the confession he just made — Jesus is the Christ, the Son of the living God.
scriptures: Matthew 16:16-18
Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God... thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church.
1 Corinthians 3:11
For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ.
Ephesians 2:20
Built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone.
corruption_summary: Used by Roman Catholic theology to ground papal succession; Reformed exegesis insists the rock is the confession of Christ, not the man.
corruption_paragraphs: The petros/petra wordplay is deliberate. Peter is the stone; the confession he makes is the bedrock. Christ Himself is the foundation; Peter is one of many living stones built upon the rock. Reformed theology preserves the apostolic centrality without making it papal.
usage: The petra is the confession; Peter is a petros.
Christ is the foundation; many living stones.

etymology: Greek euangelion (εὐαγγέλιον) — "good announcement," eu- + angelia.
biblical_def: The Greek word translated "gospel" — "good news." In imperial usage it meant tidings of military victory or royal accession; the New Testament uses it for the announcement of Christ's saving accomplishment.
webster_summary: Greek word for "good news" — gospel.
webster_full: The Greek word for 'gospel' — literally good announcement; in imperial usage it referred to tidings of military victory or royal accession; in the New Testament it became the technical term for the announcement of Christ's saving accomplishment for sinners.
scriptures: Mark 1:1
The beginning of the gospel (euangelion) of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.
Romans 1:16
For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth.
1 Corinthians 15:1-4
Moreover, brethren, I declare unto you the gospel which I preached unto you... how that Christ died for our sins... and that he was buried, and that he rose again the third day.
corruption_summary: Used so loosely that everything from social activism to therapeutic moralism gets called 'gospel.'
corruption_paragraphs: Euangelion is announcement, not advice. It is news that something has happened, not instruction in what we must do. The good news is what Christ has accomplished. Whenever the gospel becomes a to-do list, the euangelion has been lost.
usage: Preach euangelion: news, not advice.
What has been done, not what must be done.

etymology: English translation of Greek euangelion.
biblical_def: The plain-English equivalent of euangelion — the announcement that Jesus Christ died for sinners, was buried, rose on the third day, and reigns; that whoever believes in Him is saved (1 Cor 15:1-4; John 3:16).
webster_summary: The plain-English announcement of Christ's saving work.
webster_full: The plain-English term for euangelion: the announcement of what Jesus Christ has accomplished — His death for sinners, His burial, His resurrection on the third day, His exaltation, His coming return — and the call to believe and be saved.
scriptures: 1 Corinthians 15:3-4
Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures; and that he was buried, and that he rose again the third day according to the scriptures.
Romans 10:9
If thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved.
John 3:16
For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.
corruption_summary: Diluted by every brand of religious advice or political program calling itself good news.
corruption_paragraphs: The good news is news. It announces what God has done in Christ. It is not advice, lifestyle, program, or platform. Whenever 'gospel' becomes synonymous with the speaker's preferred politics or therapy, the good news has gone bad. Recover the announcement.
usage: The gospel is news, not advice.
1 Corinthians 15:1-4 gives the content.

etymology: Greek huiothesia (υἱοθεσία) — "placing as a son."
biblical_def: The legal-relational act by which God brings believers into His family as full sons and heirs, distinguished from regeneration; sealed by the Spirit who cries Abba, Father (Rom 8:15-17; Gal 4:4-7; Eph 1:5).
webster_summary: God's legal placing of believers as sons and heirs.
webster_full: The Pauline doctrine that God, through Christ and by the Spirit, brings believers into His family as full sons (and daughters) — heirs of God and joint-heirs with Christ — sealed by the Spirit's cry of 'Abba, Father.' Distinct from regeneration (new nature) and justification (legal verdict), adoption is the relational placing into the family.
scriptures: Romans 8:15
For ye have not received the spirit of bondage again to fear; but ye have received the Spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father.
Galatians 4:4-5
God sent forth his Son, made of a woman... to redeem them that were under the law, that we might receive the adoption of sons.
Ephesians 1:5
Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself.
corruption_summary: Conflated with regeneration or justification, missing the distinct relational warmth Scripture gives to adoption.
corruption_paragraphs: Adoption goes beyond pardon. The justified sinner is forgiven; the adopted son is family. The Spirit cries Abba in our hearts because the legal exchange has become a familial belonging. J. I. Packer called adoption the highest privilege of the gospel.
usage: The Spirit cries Abba; you are sons.
Adoption is the highest privilege of the gospel.

etymology: Greek synklēronomos (συγκληρονόμος) — "co-heir, joint-heir."
biblical_def: The status of every believer through adoption — heirs of God and joint-heirs with Christ, sharing in His inheritance of all things (Rom 8:17; Eph 3:6; Heb 1:2).
webster_summary: Joint-heir with Christ of all things.
webster_full: The status conferred by adoption: every believer is heir of God and joint-heir with Christ, sharing in His inheritance of all things; including suffering with Him now and being glorified with Him in the consummation.
scriptures: Romans 8:17
And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together.
Ephesians 3:6
That the Gentiles should be fellowheirs, and of the same body, and partakers of his promise in Christ by the gospel.
Hebrews 1:2
Hath in these last days spoken unto us by his Son, whom he hath appointed heir of all things.
corruption_summary: Reduced to vague heaven-talk; missing how the inheritance is real and shares in Christ's.
corruption_paragraphs: You inherit what He inherits — and He inherits all things. The inheritance is not mystical postcards; it is genuine joint-shareholding in the Son's possession of the cosmos. Romans 8:17 keeps the suffering and the glory together; do not split them.
usage: You are joint-heir with Christ.
Suffer with Him; be glorified with Him.

etymology: Greek aparchē — first portion of the harvest; applied by Paul to the risen Christ.
biblical_def: Christ's resurrection as the firstfruits of the great resurrection harvest, guaranteeing the bodily resurrection of all who belong to Him at His coming (1 Cor 15:20-23).
webster_summary: Christ's resurrection as guarantee of ours.
webster_full: Paul's image in 1 Corinthians 15: Christ's resurrection is the firstfruits — the first sheaf of a coming harvest — pledging the future resurrection of all who belong to Him at His parousia.
scriptures: 1 Corinthians 15:20
But now is Christ risen from the dead, and become the firstfruits of them that slept.
1 Corinthians 15:22-23
For as in Adam all die, even so in Christ shall all be made alive. But every man in his own order: Christ the firstfruits; afterward they that are Christ's at his coming.
Romans 8:11
But if the Spirit of him that raised up Jesus from the dead dwell in you, he that raised up Christ from the dead shall also quicken your mortal bodies.
corruption_summary: Read with Christ's resurrection as a unique miracle, missing how Paul makes it the guarantee of our bodily resurrection.
corruption_paragraphs: Christ rose first, but never alone. The firstfruits guarantee the harvest. If His resurrection is the down payment, ours is the secured purchase. Funeral hope rests not on Easter as past event but on Easter as our future reserved.
usage: Christ rose first; we rise next.
The firstfruits guarantee the harvest.
